Directing & Supervision

Directing and supervision — guiding staff, motivation, communication, discipline and supervision rounds.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe directing in nursing
  • Use supervision effectively
  • Explain motivation of staff
  • Apply discipline fairly

In simple words

Directing is telling staff what to do and supporting them to do it well. Supervision is checking that care is being given safely — kindly, specifically and with feedback.

Elements of directing

  • Clear instructions and priorities
  • Communication in both directions
  • Motivation and recognition
  • Delegation with support
  • Fair discipline
  • Role modelling

Supervision rounds

  • Check care quality: patient, notes, dressing, feeding, medication rounds
  • Watch practice: hand hygiene, infection control, drug safety
  • Supervise documentation: accuracy and completeness
  • Look at environment: lights, ventilation, safety, cleanliness
  • Record observations and corrections, then review

Motivation

  • Maslow’s hierarchy: physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation
  • Herzberg: hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction; motivators create satisfaction
  • Recognise work; provide training and career growth; involve staff in decisions

🔴 Praise in public, correct in private

Correction given in front of colleagues damages morale, while private, specific feedback protects both fairness and staff dignity.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Directing = clear duties plus support and guidance.
  2. Supervision rounds check care, records, practice and environment.
  3. Motivation theories: Maslow and Herzberg.
  4. Fairness: praise in public, correct in private.
  5. Discipline follows policy, is progressive and is documented.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Handover is part of supervision.
  2. Supervision protects patients and staff.
  3. Include staff in planning to improve commitment.
  4. Staff complaints should be heard and recorded.
  5. Appraisal links performance to development.

📌 Memory trick

Motivation: hygiene prevents dissatisfaction; motivators create satisfaction.

60-second revision

  • Direct: duty, support, motivation, corrective action.
  • Supervise: rounds, observation, records, protocol and environment.
  • Maslow and Herzberg explain staff motivation.
  • Feedback rules: praise publicly, correct privately.
  • Discipline follows policy: fair, progressive, documented.

Test yourself

Directing succeeds best when communication is:

Answer: B. Two-way, clear communication helps staff understand, ask and act correctly.

Feedback should be given:

Answer: B. Recognition is given publicly, while corrections are given privately and specifically.

Maslow’s hierarchy places safety needs after:

Answer: B. Maslow’s order: physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation.

Supervision rounds in a ward help to:

Answer: B. Supervision identifies care gaps and safety risks so they can be corrected immediately.

According to Herzberg, recognition is a:

Answer: B. Recognition and growth are motivators, whereas pay and conditions are hygiene factors.
